final_message:
I reproduced the bug and fixed it with a one-line change in `packages/reactivity/src/watch.ts`.

**Cause:** in the watcher `job`, `oldValue = newValue` only ran after the callback returned. With `flush: 'sync'`, the callback in the report sets the value back to `false`, and that runs the job again right away, inside the callback. At that point `oldValue` is still the old `false`. So the nested run compares `false` with `false`, decides nothing changed, and skips the callback. Then the outer run finishes and sets `oldValue = true`, even though the value is now `false`.

On the next click, `true` matches that `true`, so the watcher doesn't run at all and the value stays `true`. This is what the report describes.

`shallowRef` hides the problem because a shallow ref source always forces the callback to run and skips the comparison. A `computed` source, which is what the reporter uses in real code, behaves like `ref`.

**Fix:** set `oldValue = newValue` just before calling the callback instead of after. The callback still receives the previous value, because it's read into the arguments first. A nested run now compares against the value the callback is actually handling.

**Testing:**
- I added two tests: one in `packages/reactivity/__tests__/watch.spec.ts` that resets a `ref` inside its own callback, and one in `packages/runtime-core/__tests__/apiWatch.spec.ts` that uses a `computed` source with `flush: 'sync'`.
- Both failed before the fix (the callback ran once instead of twice) and pass after it.
- The full unit suite passes (3351 tests), and eslint, prettier and `pnpm check` are clean.

**Behaviour change:** in the low-level `@vue/reactivity` `watch` without the `call` option, a callback that throws now still updates `oldValue`. Before, it kept the stale value. Through `runtime-core`'s `watch`, `oldValue` was already updated after a throw, because errors are caught there, so nothing changes for normal use.
patch:
diff --git a/packages/reactivity/__tests__/watch.spec.ts b/packages/reactivity/__tests__/watch.spec.ts
index 245acfd..1a44b54 100644
--- a/packages/reactivity/__tests__/watch.spec.ts
+++ b/packages/reactivity/__tests__/watch.spec.ts
@@ -277,4 +277,29 @@ describe('watch', () => {
 
     expect(dummy).toEqual([1, 2, 3])
   })
+
+  test('should fire again after the watched ref is reset inside its own callback', () => {
+    const source = ref(false)
+    const calls: [boolean, boolean | undefined][] = []
+    watch(source, (value, oldValue) => {
+      calls.push([value, oldValue])
+      if (value) source.value = false
+    })
+
+    source.value = true
+    expect(source.value).toBe(false)
+    expect(calls).toEqual([
+      [true, false],
+      [false, true],
+    ])
+
+    source.value = true
+    expect(source.value).toBe(false)
+    expect(calls).toEqual([
+      [true, false],
+      [false, true],
+      [true, false],
+      [false, true],
+    ])
+  })
 })
diff --git a/packages/reactivity/src/watch.ts b/packages/reactivity/src/watch.ts
index 659121c..648e648 100644
--- a/packages/reactivity/src/watch.ts
+++ b/packages/reactivity/src/watch.ts
@@ -264,11 +264,11 @@ export function watch(
                 : oldValue,
             boundCleanup,
           ]
+          oldValue = newValue
           call
             ? call(cb!, WatchErrorCodes.WATCH_CALLBACK, args)
             : // @ts-expect-error
               cb!(...args)
-          oldValue = newValue
         } finally {
           activeWatcher = currentWatcher
         }
diff --git a/packages/runtime-core/__tests__/apiWatch.spec.ts b/packages/runtime-core/__tests__/apiWatch.spec.ts
index 39032a6..f9d7ee8 100644
--- a/packages/runtime-core/__tests__/apiWatch.spec.ts
+++ b/packages/runtime-core/__tests__/apiWatch.spec.ts
@@ -2010,4 +2010,22 @@ describe('api: watch', () => {
     createApp(App).mount(root)
     expect(onCleanup).toBeCalledTimes(0)
   })
+
+  // #12294
+  test('sync watcher should fire on every change when the source is reset in its callback', () => {
+    const flag = ref(false)
+    const isOn = computed(() => flag.value)
+    const spy = vi.fn((value: boolean) => {
+      if (value) flag.value = false
+    })
+    watch(isOn, spy, { flush: 'sync' })
+
+    flag.value = true
+    expect(flag.value).toBe(false)
+    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
+
+    flag.value = true
+    expect(flag.value).toBe(false)
+    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(4)
+  })
 })
